title: Process-safety correction requires barrier-health visibility, inventory/offsite-consequence discipline, and learning rails
summary: A candidate pattern for chemical/process-safety major accidents: catastrophic hazard can remain invisible under normal operations unless barrier health, inventory, offsite consequence, siting, emergency planning, mechanical integrity, and safety-critical elements are actively monitored and corrected. This is not a claim that all process-safety accidents are the same.

status_history.note: Created after promoting West Fertilizer, Imperial Sugar, Chevron Richmond, Macondo, and process-safety infrastructure records.

claims.claim: West Fertilizer, Imperial Sugar, Chevron Richmond, Macondo, and earlier BP Texas City together support a candidate process-safety pattern: low-frequency catastrophic hazards require explicit barrier-health, inventory, siting, emergency-planning, and leading-indicator disciplines because ordinary operational success or personal-safety indicators can leave major-accident risk invisible.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_refs.support_type: BP Texas City personal-safety metric trap and process-safety warning record

claims.claim: CSB, OSHA PSM, EPA RMP, and CCPS/OSHA metrics are correction or visibility rails for this pattern, but they do not prove that a given facility has complete hazard coverage, effective barrier health, or infused lessons.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: MKH-PAT-0019 must remain candidate-level because it currently has no positive control where strong process-safety indicators demonstrably intercepted a major hazard, no negative control where process-safety rails are present but not explanatory, and no recommendation-closure child records proving actual correction infusion.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The pattern is adjacent to warning-governance/proof-burden and correction-memory-versus-infusion patterns, but should not be merged until controls show whether process-safety barrier health is a distinct axis or one instance of a broader high-hazard-system family.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_profile.supporting_records: BP Texas City plus four new process-safety engineering records and four infrastructure/visibility rails.
evidence_profile.review_depth: candidate-level synthesis only; no second-pass source edition or control set.
limitations: No positive or negative controls yet.
No recommendation-closure or utilization/adoption audits yet.

positive_controls_needed: A process-safety near miss or intervention where leading indicators/barrier-health metrics demonstrably prevented escalation.
A recommendation-closure record showing CSB/PSM/RMP/CCPS-derived changes infused into procedures, inspections, design, and training before a later stressor.
negative_controls_needed: A chemical/process incident where barrier-health metrics and process-safety rails were strong and the main cause was outside this pattern.
A major release where inventory/offsite consequence was obvious but emergency planning and regulation were not the limiting factors.
counterexamples_to_seek: Cases where personal-safety metrics accurately coincided with process-safety barrier health.
Facilities with mature CCPS-style metric programs that still failed for reasons unrelated to metric/proof-burden dynamics.
Evidence that land-use, combustible dust, refinery corrosion, and offshore well control are too heterogeneous for a shared pattern.
rollback_triggers: If future controls show that the pattern collapses into MKH-PAT-0002 or MKH-PAT-0014 without process-safety-specific content.
If the pattern is used as a generalized anti-chemical-industry or anti-regulatory-policy slogan.
If second-pass reports materially revise the support records or show different dominant axes.

maturity_gate.minimum_cases: 5 support records plus 2 positive controls plus 2 negative controls plus at least 2 recommendation-closure audits
maturity_gate.required_evidence: official investigations, regulatory/program sources, leading/lagging metric evidence, recommendation closure/adoption evidence, and explicit counterexamples

handling_notes: Process-safety pattern records must preserve casualty dignity and avoid treating disasters as generic examples.
Do not use pattern labels to flatten legal, regulatory, community, or operator-context differences.

unknowns: No positive controls, negative controls, or recommendation-closure child records yet.
Current synthesis uses US-centered sources and may underrepresent non-US process-safety regimes.
No complete Bhopal/Seveso/Flixborough/Beirut international pass yet.
next_actions: Add a positive-control near-miss/intercepted hazard record.
Add recommendation-closure records for CSB recommendations from BP Texas City, West, Imperial, Chevron, and Macondo.
Add international process-safety records such as Flixborough, Seveso, and Bhopal only after strong source acquisition.
